title: Gentle Posterior Neck Stroking
summary: A very gentle introductory technique for the back of the neck, with the palms or finger pads gliding from the base of the skull toward the shoulders.
goal: Establish comfortable contact, gently warm superficial tissues, and prepare the neck and shoulder area for later techniques.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of gentle posterior neck stroking without text labels.
startingPosition: The person lies face down comfortably or sits with the arms and head supported. Keep the neck in a neutral position without extending it backward.
instructions: Place the palms or finger pads on either side of the posterior midline of the neck.
Begin with very light contact near the base of the skull.
Glide smoothly downward over the soft tissues toward the tops of the shoulders.
Near the shoulders, gently move the hands outward.
direction: The main movement travels from the base of the skull down toward the shoulders, staying on soft tissue beside the spine.
tips: Keep the neck in a neutral position.
Make the first passes especially gentle.
mistakes: Strong pressure directly over the cervical vertebrae.
Abrupt movements or extending the head backward.
Pressure on the front or side of the neck.
warning: Do not massage the front of the neck or the carotid area. Stop if pain, dizziness, numbness, or unusual symptoms occur. Neck injuries or medical conditions require professional advice.
